Definition: from G3641 and G4102; incredulous, i.e. lacking confidence (in Christ):--of little faith.
BiblicalUsage: Oligopistos means of little faith, the name Jesus gives His own disciples when they worry and fear and doubt. He asks in Matthew 6:30 and Luke 12:28 whether God will not clothe them, O ye of little faith, and in Matthew 8:26 He stills the storm after the same rebuke. Peter hears it in Matthew 14:31, sinking in the waves: O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?
TheologicalSignificance: I believe O ye of little faith is a rebuke spoken in love, because Jesus says it to His own and then stays to help them. That is why I hold that little faith is still faith, and the hand that catches Peter is the answer to every doubt.
RelatedEvents: Jesus Calms the Storm; Jesus Walks on Water
